text.p: Alphatech Electronics Plc's acting chief executive Bob Mollersteun said on Monday the troubled company had overstated its profits in at least the past three years.

Mollersteun, who replaced corporate founder Charn Uswachoke, who resigned on Monday, told reporters that the exaggerated profits were part of account discrepencies of about 10 billion baht ($322 million) that auditors Price Waterhouse found.
Mollersteun told reporters the big corporate account discrepancies had been suspected for some time. He did not elaborate.

He believed, however, that Alphatech's corporate and debt restructuring plan would still be acceptable to local and foreign creditors. "We believe that the soundness of the plan is such that it will gain bondholder approval," Mollersteun said earlier in a statement.
The statement said the company would keep to its schedule of briefing holders of its eurobonds in Zurich on August 6.
The ailing firm had failed to meet a July 7 payment deadline to bondholders who had on June 27 exercised a put option on $43.68 million of the firm's total $45 million euroconvertible loans.

Alphatech on Monday asked the Thai bourse to suspend its shares because the company was informed by auditors Price Waterhouse of "a number of improper transactions which affect the company's reported accounts".
Mollersteun said in his statement: "I want to reassure our customers and employees that the findings in the Price Waterhouse audit do not affect the day to day operations of the company."
Alphatech's chief financial officer Lislie Merszei also told reporters that his firm was saddled with a total outstanding debt of about $400 million.

"There have been two separate sets of problems. The first set is related party transactions and the second set is the restating of previous year earnings. Both problems are somewhere in the region of 10 billion baht," he said.
